title: The Storyteller's Voice
text:
In many nineteenth-century novels, the narrator speaks directly to the reader, offering commentary on the characters and their motives. This technique, known as intrusive narration, allows the author to guide judgments without revealing everything at once. Readers therefore encounter a voice that seems knowledgeable, yet is sometimes deliberately selective. Such narrators can be charming, irritating, or even misleading.

Modern critics have paid close attention to these narrative choices. By contrasting the narrator's account with the events that the characters actually experience, they can detect gaps between what is said and what is meant. Some authors exploit those gaps for irony, while others use them to build suspense. Consequently, a careful reader learns to question the storyteller as well as the story.

questions.text: According to the passage, what is intrusive narration?
options: A narrator who speaks directly to the reader and comments on the characters
A story told entirely through letters between characters
A narrator who never reveals the thoughts of any character
A technique that removes all commentary from a novel

questions.text: According to the passage, how can critics detect gaps in a narrator's account?
options: By reading the novel aloud to a group
By comparing the narrator's account with what characters actually experience
By counting how many chapters the narrator controls
By ignoring the narrator's commentary completely

questions.text: What can be inferred about a narrator who is described as 'deliberately selective'?
options: They always tell the complete truth in every chapter
They may leave out details that would change how readers judge events
They have no effect on how readers view the characters
They appear only in twentieth-century novels

questions.text: Why does the passage suggest that a careful reader should question the storyteller?
options: Because all modern novels are written in the first person
Because critics have banned intrusive narration
Because the narrator's perspective can shape what the reader believes
Because suspense depends only on the reader's age

vocabulary.definition: interfering or inserting oneself into something uninvited
choosing carefully, often leaving some things out
a contrast between what is expected or said and what is actually meant or happens
a state of uncertain anticipation about what will happen next

paragraph_translations: On dokuzuncu yüzyıl romanlarının birçoğunda anlatıcı okuyucuyla doğrudan konuşur ve karakterlerin ile onların niyetleri üzerine yorumlar yapar. Yazarın her şeyi bir anda ortaya koymadan yargıları yönlendirmesine olanak tanıyan bu teknik, müdahaleci anlatım olarak bilinir. Bu nedenle okuyucular bilgili görünen, ama bazen kasıtlı olarak seçici davranan bir sesle karşılaşırlar. Bu tür anlatıcılar büyüleyici, sinir bozucu ya da hatta yanıltıcı olabilir.

Modern eleştirmenler bu anlatım tercihlerine yakından dikkat etmiştir. Anlatıcının aktarımını karakterlerin gerçekte yaşadığı olaylarla karşılaştırarak, söylenen ile kastedilen arasındaki boşlukları fark edebilirler. Bazı yazarlar bu boşlukları ironi için kullanırken, diğerleri gerilim yaratmak için kullanır. Sonuç olarak dikkatli bir okuyucu, hikâyenin kendisi kadar onu anlatanı da sorgulamayı öğrenir.
